message.content:
This appears to be a CBP ruling on bulletin board borders made of paperboard. The likely candidates are 4911.99 (other printed matter), 4823.90 (other paper and paperboard cut to size or shape), or 4905 and 9505 (festive articles), none of which fits cleanly.

The die-cut apples are shaped paperboard where the printing is secondary, which points to 4823.90. The other two borders are printed with decorative patterns, so the printing is not secondary, and Chapter 49 printed matter (4911.99) could apply. However, the ruling covers all three products and likely gives them a single classification.

Chapter 48 Note 12 (paper and paperboard of headings 4801, 4802, 4803, 4805, 4808 etc.) covers printed goods only when the printing is not the primary use. Printed decorative borders are classified in 4911.99 only if the printing is the essential feature, since Chapter 49 covers printed matter in which printing is primary. Here the printing is decorative and tied to the border's use. Note 12 to Chapter 49 excludes articles of 4823 only if the printing is incidental to the primary use. Because the die-cut shape is the key feature of the first border, and the others are coated paperboard cut to shape with a wavy edge or rectangular pieces, 4823.90 fits the set. Printed patterns on the other two borders are decorative, not informational, so they are also classified in 4823.90.

The 4823.90 subheading's statistical suffix for "other" is 4823.90.8600 (other, not in 4823.90.85 breakouts). The current numbering has 4823.90.8500 for paper or paperboard of a kind used for writing, printing or graphic purposes and 4823.90.8600 for other. The calcium carbonate coated paperboard is more probably classed as 4823.90.8600.
